items.title: Michael White interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 10, 2025
items.q: they featured you know some of the great modern jazz musicians in New Orleans like Ellis Marsalis

ctx.x: I’m sure you have an updated – there’s an updated version that they probably have a larger thing on you.

Yeah I’ll have to check it out. But yeah, you know it’s a funny thing. I listened to a lot of different music before I got to the authentic New Orleans jazz style and sound. The first jazz I actually heard was bebop because there was a little of that on the radio and they used to have live broadcasts from this place called Lou and Charlie’s and they featured you know some of the great modern jazz musicians in New Orleans like Ellis Marsalis and, you know, people like that. And I used to listen to those things.…
Did you hear Buddy DeFranco at the time?

items.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: the only bandleader that in know of in this town who’s a clarinet player is Michael White.

ctx.x: Why do you think that is?

It’s a couple of reasons. For one thing, the band programs in the school that used to have those real great band teachers, they ain’t there no more. The next thing is, if given a choice between clarinet and saxophone, most of them kids will take saxophone, but clarinet’s hard. And there’s no leadership – the only bandleader that in know of in this town who’s a clarinet player is Michael White. Michael White was sort of a disciple of – can’t think of the old man’s name.
